# cache

Everything in Redis. Top-level because the worker and the kie.ai client need it too.

- `redis.py` — `get_redis()`: **the only Redis connection in the repo**, URL-keyed lazy global (rebuilt when `OFM_REDIS_URL` changes). `get_text`/`set_text`/`delete_text` are for optimisation caches only: they swallow `RedisError` as a miss. Anything that must not lose a write uses `get_redis()` and picks its own failure policy.
- `queue.py` — `JobQueue(QueueName.X)`: a FIFO line on RQ, `.put(fn, ...)` joins the back, `.line()` says who waits and how many are ahead; `enqueue(fn, ...)` / `enqueue_to(queue, fn, ...)` are `put` for short. Which queues exist, their worker counts and priority: `config/settings.py` (`QueueName`, `InfraSettings.queues`). Tests (`OFM_RQ_ASYNC=false`) run it inline. Queues: `default` (compose `worker`, `OFM_RQ_WORKERS` 10), `clone-links` (/clone-links runs, compose `clone-links-worker`, `OFM_CLONE_LINKS_WORKERS` 5: a 120-link Generate never holds the default queue), `previews` (`preview-worker`, 1), `media` (`media-worker`, `OFM_MEDIA_WORKERS` 1: big local encodes, one at a time). Each is `python -m ofmhelpers.worker [queue]`. `JOB_QUEUES` = the queues `run_job` goes on. `active_job_ids()` (recovery's view of live jobs; None = unknown) reads, in the order a job moves, each job queue's list, then its `:intermediate` list (rq BLMOVEs a dequeued job there before the horse sets `current_job`), then every worker's `current_job` -- read in another order, a job just being dequeued was missed and failed as cut off (review #57).

Callers: every background-job router (`enqueue`); repository cache, rate limits, `features/assets/ref_usage.py` (`get_redis`); kie.ai upload memo (`get_text`/`set_text`).
